message: Astra wins by two points; the real story is cached input pricing
yt_title: GPT-6 Astra: wins by 2 points, but cached inputs change everything
yt_desc:
OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra on September 3rd, 2026. The numbers underneath it are the real story.

1.05 million token context window. 128,000 output tokens in a single generation.

On Terminal Bench 4.0 Astra scored 57.9% on complex software engineering tasks. Claude Fable 5.1 scored 55.8%. It wins — by two points.

Pricing: $10 per million input tokens, $50 per million output. But cache your inputs and it drops to $1 per million. That's where the economics actually change.

Full breakdown on the channel.

lines.text: OpenAI launched GPT six Astra on September the third, and the numbers underneath it are the actual story.
A one point zero five million token context window, and a hundred and twenty eight thousand output tokens in a single generation.
On Terminal Bench four, Astra scored fifty seven point nine percent on complex software engineering tasks.
Claude Fable five point one scored fifty five point eight. So Astra wins, but it wins by two points.
Ten dollars per million input tokens. Fifty dollars per million output. That is the sticker price.
But cache your inputs and it drops to one dollar per million. That is where the economics actually change.
